items.item:
1. Two concurrent publishes of `estimate` on one project, with different
   request ids, make versions n+1 and
   n+2, the first `superseded`, the second `published`; neither answers an
   internal error.
   Shows A07-1, A07-2, A07-3, A07-4. [witness: verification:registry_a07_concurrent_publishes_consecutive_versions]
statements:
for each project p and type t:
  count(pointer of p, t with status published) <= 1   -- A07-1
versions of p, t are 1..n without gaps or repeats   -- A07-2

publish(p, t) accepted:
  new.version = max(version of p, t) + 1 (or 1)   -- A07-3
previous published of p, t becomes superseded in the same transaction   -- A07-4

verdicts.item:
1. Two concurrent publishes of `estimate` on one project, with different
   request ids, make versions n+1 and
   n+2, the first `superseded`, the second `published`; neither answers an
   internal error.
   Shows A07-1, A07-2, A07-3, A07-4. [witness: verification:registry_a07_concurrent_publishes_consecutive_versions]
statements:
for each project p and type t:
  count(pointer of p, t with status published) <= 1   -- A07-1
versions of p, t are 1..n without gaps or repeats   -- A07-2

publish(p, t) accepted:
  new.version = max(version of p, t) + 1 (or 1)   -- A07-3
previous published of p, t becomes superseded in the same transaction   -- A07-4
quotes: assert sum(1 for p in pointers if p["status"] == "published") <= 1
verdicts.why: The test asserts both concurrent publishes are accepted and changed, receive consecutive versions, leave a contiguous history with at most one published pointer, and leave the preceding pointers superseded. It does not observe or fault the publish operation to establish that superseding the previous pointer and publishing the new one occur in the same transaction, so A07-4 is only asserted in its final-state form.
